findings.what: This arm also fires when a read fails after `drain`'s wait has already reaped the child (or when the wait itself failed with ECHILD), so `kill_group(leader)` can then name a pgid the OS has handed to an unrelated process group, which is the exact hazard the comment says the ordering avoids; the sweep should be gated on the child not yet having been reaped (e.g. `child.try_wait()` returning `Ok(None)`).
